one_liner: Cloud data warehouse with a REST SQL API and Snowflake REST APIs for managing resources; you sign up yourself for a 30-day free trial.
notes: Auth for the Snowflake REST APIs: key pair authentication (signed JWT, so other), OAuth (Snowflake OAuth / External OAuth authorization flows, so oauth2), programmatic access token (PAT, a static token created by the user, so api_key), and workload identity federation (other). The SQL API page lists OAuth, key pair and workload identity federation, and also accepts PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN as a token type. Password/Basic is not offered for these HTTP APIs. Access: self-service sign-up needs only an email, with no payment information, and gives a 30-day trial with free credits. After that the account is suspended unless you upgrade, so access=self_serve_trial. I labelled the verdict ready (you get self-serve credentials and the API is documented) with main_blocker none. The ambiguity is that lasting use needs a paid account, so someone could argue for paid_plan as the blocker. MCP is official: the Snowflake-managed MCP server is documented on docs.snowflake.com (CREATE MCP SERVER object), and Snowflake-Labs/mcp also exists on GitHub. Breadth is broad: you can run any SQL through the SQL API plus CRUD on databases, warehouses, users, roles, tasks and more through the REST APIs.

evidence.quote: The trial continues for 30 days (from the sign-up date)
At the end of the trial, the account is suspended.
The Snowflake SQL API is a REST API that you can use to access and update data in a Snowflake database.
The Snowflake-managed MCP server lets AI agents securely retrieve data from Snowflake accounts without needing to deploy separate infrastructure.
no payment information or other qualifying information is required
